answer: Trademark binding: each agent is tied to a live registered trademark. Validators look up the registration number in the trademark office's public register, check that it is active and that the owner matches, then confirm a one-time code posted on the mark's specimen page, say for an Onyx Knoll Meadow label. One registration maps to one identity. An extra identity needs its own filing fee and months of examination, and the office refuses near-duplicate marks, so splitting cannot reuse one. Limit: it excludes small operators, and lax registries sell cheap marks, so offices must be whitelisted.
